AUTHOR: Villon
TITLE: Toward an artificial intelligence-assisted counting of sharks on baited video
SPECIES: Target: Carcharhinus amblyrhynchos, C. melanopterus, Triaenodon obesus (model trained on 8 shark + 19 non-shark species)
DATA: Own 185 one-hour BRUVS videos (Videostations) and 1366 15-20 s clips (Videoclips, 23,222 frames)
D_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'Using a 80% training/20% testing random split on videos rather than images ensured full independency between images of the training set and testing set.'
R_EV: Sec. 1.1: 'We collected one-hour baited videos (BRUVS) at 185 different stations across New-Caledonia's reefs'
C_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'we manually reviewed the network's annotations, making corrections where necessary'; Table 2 precision 0.76/0.58/0.23 automated vs 1 semi-automated
E_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'Correlation and linear regression analyses were then used to compare MaxN predicted by the models with MaxN observed by biologists.'
ARCH: Faster R-CNN with NASNet backbone (TF2 faster_rcnn_nas)
METR: precision, recall, F-measure; MaxN correlation R, regression slope/intercept, MaxN accuracy
NOTE: Testingstations (22 whole 1-h videos) fully independent; but Testingclips are clips randomly split from the same 163 training videos, so clip-level test may share source videos with training (verifier check). All stations from one New Caledonia campaign -> R1=N. No detection score threshold reported (C1=NR). C5 coded from semi-automated manual review of all test detections with precision before/after; also a 2-consecutive-frame consistency rule to suppress false-positive MaxN (not ID-switch handling). Recall reported but FNR/size-class not -> E4=없음; small/far individuals discussed qualitatively. TAXA coded as 3 target species though model has 27 classes.
